data.one_liner: Library for parsing raw command-line arguments into options and values using GNU and POSIX styles.
data.what_it_does: Parses raw command-line arguments into typed options, flags, and multi-options following GNU and POSIX standards. It also supports structuring command-line applications with commands, subcommands, and automated help text generation via a CommandRunner class.
use_when: You are building a command-line interface (CLI) application in Dart.
You need to parse flags, options, and multi-options with default values and validation.
You want to structure a CLI app with nested commands and automatic help generation.
avoid_when: You are building a purely graphical or web user interface without command-line input.
You require complex positional grammar that cannot be modeled by standard GNU/POSIX flags and commands.
strengths: Supports both GNU and POSIX style options and flags.
Built-in Command and CommandRunner classes for structured CLI apps with automatic help menus.
Robust validation including allowed values and mandatory options.
weaknesses: Imperative approach requires manually setting up parsers and commands in code.
